on_shared_budget_exhaustion: discard concurrently produced graph; retain deterministic discovery diagnostics
policy_basis: Versioned bounded defaults; not claimed as production sizing evidence

result_memory.unit: logical working-set estimate, not Go heap or RSS
result_memory.shared_once: POM analysis cache keys and identical material ids
derived_caps: encoding/json and encoding/xml decoder internals: SizeDecoderScratch (4KiB) charged per Parse/Decode in addition to Working of the document; not a measurement of decoder heap
RPM live page make([]byte,n) is gated by MaxReadBytes/MaxPageVisits; Parse also charges SizeOfBytes(min(MaxRecordBytes,16MiB)) as a conservative peak page/header working set
pipeline materials.Open 32KiB read scratch is Once-charged as snapshot-read-scratch
fillReport sort indexes charge SizePtr per package/location/requirement before sort.SliceStable; comparator temporary clones in locationKey/requirementKey are still sort runtime

MergePackages keeps the old no-error signature and uses budget.From(background) default MaxResultBytes; exhaustion returns the original slice unchanged (not nil). MergePackagesBudget charges pointer-set/index maps, extra License/FromFile/FromAnalyzer/MergeDetails copies, collected edges, rebuilt graphs, and the output index before any input mutation; same pointers are visited once
unbounded_runtime: Go decoder reflection into caller structs after SizeDecoderScratch
locktoml node.value() map rebuild after per-token charges; json.Marshal conversion is charged as Working of the JSON bytes
sort.Slice comparator closures may allocate extra index copies beyond SizeOfSortIndex
Go map bucket growth beyond SizeMap/SizePtr; GC, stack, and RSS are not this estimate

strict_preallocation_status: Shared MaxResultBytes is a logical working-set estimate charged before documented working copies, nodes, enqueue, merge inserts, and report appends. Decoder scratch, RPM page peak, snapshot read scratch, and sort indexes now have conservative charges derived from existing byte/node limits. This is not a strict pre-allocation or RSS cap. Remaining runtime overhead is named in result_memory.unbounded_runtime.
